title: Tracking the neurodevelopmental trajectory of beta band oscillations with optically pumped magnetometer-based magnetoencephalography
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Original Appendix2 comparison of scalp-to-sensor proximity for actual adaptable helmets versus a virtual non-adaptable largest helmet on the same participant heads. Recover this exact geometric comparison; age–beta association is descriptive calibration and not the ordered performance target.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Original Appendix2 comparison of scalp-to-sensor proximity for actual adaptable helmets versus a virtual non-adaptable largest helmet on the same participant heads. Recover this exact geometric comparison; age–beta association is descriptive calibration and not the ordered performance target.

Source-paper comparison for Original Appendix2 per-participant mean sensor-to-scalp Euclidean distance; source-compatible primary panel/summary unresolved: For sensor s and participant i, distance is the minimum Euclidean distance from its vapor-cell center to that participant scalp surface; the source averages sensor distances within each participant. Lower distance is ordered only under the same valid physical geometry/support. Age/head-circumference correlations and slopes are separate source panels, not substitute improvement rewards.
success_criteria: Recover the original participant head models, sensor positions/counts, largest-head reference, rigid transforms, distance vectors and complete actual-versus-virtual Appendix2 comparison.

Establish that a feasible computational candidate domain exists under the same source physical/acquisition conditions before defining an improvement episode; no free coordinate movement, new hardware, altered head cohort or unconstrained closer placement is admitted.

Compare against the source adaptable system, not only the weaker simulated fixed-size helmet; preserve all original proximity and head-size conditions with a justified primary summary and meaningful uncertainty rule.
A higher age–beta R², lower biological p-value, different neural predictor, novel helmet acquisition or invented aggregate does not surpass the original geometric comparison.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
